route: The promise problem: is deciding val(v0) >= 1/2 + eps against <= 1/2 - eps polynomial for eps = 1/poly, target-equivalent, or neither provably
object: The GAP-AMPLIFYING CONTEXT as a Boolean-analysis object: a context of def:gate, plugged with a game, is a bounded function of one independent Bernoulli(p) variable per call, and its amplification is the total influence of that function -- so the amplification available at a given size is a Fourier/Bessel quantity, and the CYCLE STRUCTURE OF THE CALL DIGRAPH (which the paper had only used to ask whether a composite is stopping) is exactly what decides whether the cost of amplifying a gap delta is 1/delta or 1/delta^2.
headline: For every eps >= 1/poly(N) the promise problems Gap_eps, App_eps and Ord_eps are polynomial-time equivalent to Gap_{1/4}: the open middle of the eps-ladder of rem:eps-ladder is a single problem.

results.name: The middle of the eps-ladder collapses
results.statement: Let eps(N) in (0,1/4] be nonincreasing, polynomial-time computable and bounded below by 1/q(N) for a polynomial q. Then Gap_eps reduces to Gap_{1/4} by a polynomial-time MANY-ONE reduction of promise problems, namely G -> A_k(G) with A_0(G)=G, A_j(G) = M<A_{j-1}(G)> for the four-call majority context M of def:pg-maj and k = ceil(ln(1/(4 eps))/ln(11/8)); the image is a stopping SSG on at most eps^{-4.36} N vertices. Since Gap_{1/4} reduces to Gap_eps by the identity, all Gap_eps with eps >= 1/poly are many-one equivalent to Gap_{1/4}, and with rem:eps-ladder's four reductions so are App_eps and Ord_eps (Turing equivalence, those being adaptive). Equivalently: SSG-Value restricted to instances with |val(v0)-1/2| >= 1/4 and SSG-Value restricted to instances with |val(v0)-1/2| >= N^{-c} are polynomial-time equivalent for every constant c.
results.why_not_implied: rem:eps-ladder proves interreducibility only UP TO A CONSTANT FACTOR in eps and explicitly leaves "1/poly(N), or 1/4" as two forms of one undecided question; the only amplifier it points at (through rem:no-amplification) is the gambler's-ruin chain, whose composite with a two-player game NEED NOT BE STOPPING -- so lem:gate does not apply to it and it is not a legal reduction between problems posed on stopping games; the collapse needs an amplifier that is acyclic, which is a construction and not a three-line consequence.
results.argument: M is the short-circuited majority-of-three decision tree, four call vertices q0->(q1,q1'), q1->(t1,q2), q1'->(q2,t0), q2->(t1,t0). M has no directed cycle, so it is admissible and M<G> is stopping (a trap of the composite would give a trap of G or a cycle of M, lem:trapchar). Backwards through M^{p,q} the first exit always carries the larger value (1 >= p, p >= 0, 2p-p^2 >= p^2), so by lem:gate every gate is read on its p-branch and q never enters: val(M<G>) = p(2p-p^2) + (1-p)p^2 = 3p^2-2p^3 =: g(p). g is nondecreasing, g(1/2)=1/2, g(1-p)=1-g(p), and g(1/2+d)-1/2 = (3/2)d - 2d^3, which is >= d for d <= 1/2 and >= (11/8)d for d <= 1/4. Hence the gap multiplies by at least 11/8 per level until it reaches 1/4 and never falls back, so k = ceil(ln(1/(4eps))/ln(11/8)) levels give value >= 3/4 (resp. <= 1/4 by the symmetry). Size 4^k(N-2)+2 with 4^k <= 4(4eps)^{-ln4/ln(11/8)} = 4(4eps)^{-4.3533} <= 0.01 eps^{-4.36}; k = O(log N) since eps >= 1/q(N), so the map is polynomial-time. Outside the promise the reduction may do anything, which is what a many-one reduction of promise problems requires.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout. The composite is BUILT AS A GAME (mycore.G) and checked from the game: stopping by the trap test of lem:trapchar, and the claimed value vector shown to be a fixed point of T -- unique on a stopping game by thm:contraction. t_amp.py: G = two dyadic coin chains and a two-player game (1 max, 1 min, val 3/4), k=1,2,3, composites of 12..384 non-sinks, val = g^{(k)}(p) in every case. t_rec.py: the recursive A_k, k=1..5 on the two-player game, composites 16,64,256,1024,4096 non-sinks, all matching. t_bf.py: BRUTE FORCE over all 2^4 x 2^4 positional pairs of the 16-vertex two-player composite gives 27/32 = g(3/4). t_gm.py: G = G_m of thm:vi-lower, m=3,4,5, k=1..4, composites 24..2560 non-sinks; G_3 (delta = 1/16) first exceeds 3/4 at k=4. Level counts (levels.txt, delta iterated with rounding DOWN to 200 bits so the counts are certified): delta = 2^-3..2^-16 needs k* = 2,4,6,8,9,11,13,14,16,18,19,21,23,25 against the proved bound 3,5,7,9,11,14,16,18,20,22,24,27,29,31 -- k* <= bound at every size; log(4^k*)/log(1/delta) rises to 3.125 at 2^-16, towards the asymptotic log4/log(3/2) = 3.4190. Games dumped: AMP_G4_k1.json (n=32, val 8959/16384 = g(17/32)), AMP_G4_k2.json (n=128), AMP_G4_k3.json (n=512); verify_pg.py re-reads them and recomputes the value independently.

results.name: Acyclic amplifiers pay a square (the influence bound)
results.statement: Call a context H acyclic if no directed cycle of H passes through a call. (a) For an acyclic H with s calls and any vertex v, V(p) := val(H^{p,p})(v) is continuous and piecewise polynomial on [0,1] and |V'(p)| <= sqrt(s)/(2 sqrt(p(1-p))) wherever it exists. (b) Consequently, if H is acyclic with s calls and val(H<G>)(v) >= 3/4 whenever val_G(v0) >= 1/2+delta and <= 1/4 whenever val_G(v0) <= 1/2-delta (0 < delta <= 1/4), then s >= 3/(64 delta^2) > 1/(22 delta^2). Since rem:no-amplification's gambler's-ruin context attains s = Theta(1/delta), an optimal amplifier must have a call on a directed cycle: cyclicity of the call digraph is necessary for amplification cheaper than delta^{-2}.
results.why_not_implied: rem:no-amplification bounds |dV/dp| by (s+3)/(4p(1-p)) through thm:energy's crossing inequality -- LINEAR in s, and it is tight, being attained by the ruin chain; nothing there separates acyclic from cyclic contexts, and its bound cannot give delta^{-2} because the bound itself is only delta^{-1}. The square comes from a different mechanism (each call is read at most once, so the composite is a bounded function of s independent Bernoulli variables and its derivative is the total influence, bounded by sqrt(s) via Bessel), which the paper does not use anywhere.
results.argument: Fix a positional pair (sigma,tau) at H's max and min vertices; the gates are chance vertices. Acyclicity means a play enters each call at most once, so the process can be realised by drawing in advance one independent X_c ~ Bern(p) per call, the call leaving through e_1 iff X_c = 1; the context's own average coins are independent of X. Let h(x) = Pr[reach t1 | X = x] in [0,1], so V_{sigma,tau}(p) = E_p h(X). Differentiating the product measure coordinatewise, V'_{sigma,tau}(p) = sum_c E[d_c h] with d_c h = h(x^{c->1}) - h(x^{c->0}). With chi_c := (x_c - p)/sqrt(p(1-p)) one has E[h chi_c] = sqrt(p(1-p)) E[d_c h] (condition on x off c), and {1, chi_c} is orthonormal, so Bessel gives sum_c E[h chi_c]^2 <= Var(h) <= 1/4; Cauchy-Schwarz then gives |sum_c E[d_c h]| <= sqrt(s)/(2 sqrt(p(1-p))). No monotonicity of h is needed. Finally V = max_sigma min_tau V_{sigma,tau} (thm:determinacy) is a max-min of finitely many polynomials; off the finitely many roots of their pairwise differences the ordering is constant, so V agrees locally with one member -- whence continuity, piecewise polynomiality and the bound. For (b): player-free games realise every dyadic value (lem:dyadic-row) and V is continuous, so V(1/2+delta) >= 3/4 and V(1/2-delta) <= 1/4; on the interval p(1-p) >= 1/4 - delta^2 >= 3/16, so 1/2 <= integral of V' <= 2 delta sqrt(s)/(2 sqrt(3/16)) = (4/sqrt3) delta sqrt(s).
results.verification: t_infl.py: 4000 random ACYCLIC contexts (max/min/avg/call vertices, up to 7 calls, all edges pointing forward), values computed exactly by backward induction in Fractions, difference quotients at p = 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4 with step 10^-5. Maximum of |V'| / (sqrt(s)/(2 sqrt(p(1-p)))) over all of them is exactly 1.0, attained by the one-call context V(p) = p at p = 1/2 -- so the bound holds everywhere and is tight. The majority tower has s = 4^k calls and V'(1/2) = (3/2)^k, measured 1.5, 2.25, 3.375, 5.0625, 7.5937, 11.3906 for k = 1..6 against the bound 2^k = 2,4,8,16,32,64.

results.name: The ruin amplifier is exact for every plug
results.statement: Let R_K be the context with calls b_1..b_K, b_i -> (b_{i+1}, b_{i-1}), b_0 = t_0, b_{K+1} = t_1, and let G be any STOPPING SSG with start v0 and p = val_G(v0). Then, whether or not R_K<G> is stopping, val(R_K<G>)(b_i) = (1-r^i)/(1-r^{K+1}) with r = (1-p)/p (and i/(K+1) at p = 1/2). Consequently, if arbitrary SSGs are admitted as instances, Gap_eps reduces many-one to Gap_{1/4} by a reduction of size O(N/eps): take K+1 = 2h with h = ceil(ln3/(3 eps)) and start at b_h.
results.why_not_implied: rem:no-amplification computes the ruin values ONLY for a player-free plug, and explicitly records that with a two-player G the composite need not be stopping, leaving the value of that composite unaddressed; lem:gate, its only tool for reading a composite, presupposes the composition is stopping. The statement here is that the ruin value survives exactly when the composite has a trap, proved by a coupling and not by lem:gate.
results.argument: Let sigma* be optimal for Max in G and let Max play it in every copy. G is stopping, so every entry leaves its copy almost surely, and by the Markov property the successive exits of the copy at b_i are independent with one fixed probability P_i of leaving through e_1; val_{sigma*} >= p forces P_i >= p. The induced state process is a birth-and-death walk on {0..K+1} with up-probabilities P_i >= p > 0, absorbed almost surely (K+1 consecutive up-steps have probability at least p^{K+1} from anywhere), whose ruin probability (sum_{j<i} pi_j)/(sum_{j<K+1} pi_j), pi_j = prod_{l<=j}(1-P_l)/P_l, is nondecreasing in every P_l; hence val >= the display. Playing tau* optimal for Min in every copy gives P_i <= p and the reverse. For the reduction, ln r = ln(1-2d) - ln(1+2d) <= -4d + 2d^2 <= -3d for d <= 1/2, so r^h <= 1/3 once 3 d h >= ln 3, and the value at b_h is 1/(1+r^h) >= 3/4; symmetrically <= 1/4 below.
results.verification: t_ruin.py builds R_K<G> as a real game and computes its value by BRUTE FORCE over all positional pairs (mycore.wstar, whose profile evaluation is trap-aware and therefore correct on non-stopping games). Player-free G of value 3/4, K = 2,3,4,5: composite stopping, formula exact at every state. Two-player G (1 max, 1 min, value 3/4), K = 2..5: stopping, formula exact. The two-player game 0 max->(1,3), 1 min->(t1,2), 2 avg->(t0,t0), 3 avg->(t1,t0) of value 1/2: for K = 2,3,4,5,6 the composite (n = 8,12,16,20,24) is NOT stopping -- the copies at b_i and b_{i+1}, each driven out through one exit, form a trap, exactly the failure rem:no-amplification predicts -- and the value is i/(K+1) at every state all the same.

results.name: No value-iteration scheme approximates: the well
results.statement: For even K and 1 <= m <= K-1 let WELL(K,m) be the player-free stopping SSG on the 2(K-1) average vertices A_i, B_i realising a birth-and-death walk on states 0..K (0 = t0, K = t1) with up-probability 3/4 below m and 1/4 from m on, started at A_m; N = 2K, a = N-2. Then val(A_m) = (sum_{j<m} pi_j)/(sum_{j<K} pi_j) with pi_j = prod_{l<=j} r_l, r_l = 1/3 for l <= m-1 and 3 for l >= m; in particular WELL^-(K) := WELL(K,K/2) has val = 1/4 EXACTLY and WELL^+(K) := WELL(K,K/2+1) has val = (3/4)(1-3^{-m})/(1-3^{1-m}) > 3/4. With h := min(m,K-m) and Q := 3^{h-1}/16 = 2^{Omega(N)}: (a) (T^k 0)(A_m) < 1/4 for every k < Q; (b) (T^k 1)(A_m) - (T^k 0)(A_m) > 1/2 for every k < Q; (c) the stopping-probability path of def:discount-path has val_rho(A_m) < 1/4 for every rho with 1-rho >= 68*3^{-(h-1)}, in particular for every 1-rho = 1/poly(N). Hence one-sided value iteration, two-sided value iteration and the damped family give the SAME verdict on a Gap_{1/4} YES-instance (val > 3/4) and on a Gap_{1/4} NO-instance (val = 1/4): no decision rule reading only them decides Gap_{1/4} at any polynomial budget -- already with Vmax = Vmin = empty.
results.why_not_implied: thm:vi-lower's G_m has val(c_1) = 1/2 + 2^{-(m+1)}, so it satisfies NO promise: a Gap_{1/4} or App_{1/4} algorithm is allowed to answer anything on it, and the constant 1/2 is already an App_{1/4} answer produced by zero iterations. Its statement is therefore about the exact bit, not about approximation, and it says nothing about the damped family or about a two-sided bracket. WELL has a constant gap, and the failure of the three schemes there is a failure at eps = 1/4.
results.argument: Each state's two average vertices realise the biased step exactly (1/2 + 1/2*1/2 = 3/4, resp. 1/4), so the states form the stated birth-and-death chain and the displayed ruin formula is its absorption probability; summing the two geometric series gives exactly 6(1-3^{-m}) for m = K/2 with numerator (3/2)(1-3^{-m}), i.e. exactly 1/4, and (3/4)(1-3^{-m})/(1-3^{1-m}) > 3/4 for m = K/2+1. From A_m the chain steps to m-1 with probability 3/4 and to m+1 with 1/4; on {0..m} every state has up-probability 3/4, so with rho = 1/3 the ruin probability from m-1 is (rho^{m-1}-rho^m)/(1-rho^m) <= 3^{-(m-1)}, and symmetrically from m+1 it is at most 3^{-(K-m-1)}: the probability q of reaching a sink before returning to A_m is at most 2*3^{-(h-1)}. Each excursion takes at least one step, so at most k+1 excursions begin within k steps and each is absorbing with probability q, whence Pr[absorbed within k] <= (k+1)q. Now (T^k 0)(v) = Pr[t1 within k steps] <= (k+1)q < 1/4 for k < Q, and (T^k 1)(v) >= Pr[no sink within k] >= 1-(k+1)q, so the bracket width exceeds 1-2(k+1)q > 1/2 on the same range. For (c), val_rho <= E[rho^tau] <= Pr[tau <= k] + rho^k <= (k+1)q + e^{-(1-rho)k}; taking k = floor(1/(16q)) gives (k+1)q <= 1/16 + q, and (1-rho)k >= ln 8 as soon as 1-rho >= 34q, so val_rho <= 1/16 + q + 1/8 < 1/4.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic; every instance built as a game (well.py) and checked from the game: stopping by the trap test, and the exact value vector shown to be a fixed point of T; the ruin formula independently cross-checked by a linear solve on the game (verify_pg.py). Sizes K = 4,6,8,10,12,14,16 (n = 6..30). Values of WELL^+: 13/16, 10/13, 121/160, 91/121, 1093/1456, 820/1093, 9841/13120, decreasing to 3/4; WELL^- gives 1/4 exactly at every size. Measured first k with (T^k 0)(v0) >= 1/4: 2, 19, 68, 216, 661, 1991, 5983; with >= 1/2: 9, 49, 178, 575, 1772, 5373, 16181; first k with two-sided bracket width < 1/2: 8, 34, 117, 368, 1125, 3398; width < 1/4: 14, 66, 229, 729, 2239, 6782 -- consecutive ratios tending to 3 per Delta K = 2, i.e. the law 3^{N/4} = 2^{0.396 N}. Damped path at K = 14 (w* = 0.7502): rho = 1-2^-2, ..., 1-2^-10 gives 0.0000, 0.0010, 0.0079, 0.0355, 0.1284. Games dumped: WELL_hi_K14.json (n = 26, val 820/1093) and WELL_lo_K14.json (n = 26, val 1/4).

results.name: The up-rounded grid iteration returns the trivial bound below the denominator
results.statement: Let y_D be the least fixed point of ceil_D o T reached from 0 on the uniform grid of mesh 1/D; it is reached in at most ND monotone rounds and satisfies w* <= y_D (from T y_D <= y_D and cor:comparison), so it is a polynomial-time computable upper bound whenever D = poly(N). MEASURED, NOT PROVED: on WELL^-(K), where w*(v0) = 1/4 exactly, y_D(v0) >= 1/2 for every mesh D below 3^{K/2} = 3^{N/4} and y_D(v0) < 1/2 for every tested D at or above it -- the threshold is exactly the denominator of the values, so the scheme is useless below it and exact at it (thm:alphabet-iteration). The general error identity is y_D - w* = (I-M)^{-1} rho with rho_v in {0, 1/(2D)} at every average vertex and rho_v = 0 at every controlled one, the max and the min of two grid points being grid points.
results.why_not_implied: cor:grid-iteration assumes D val(v) is an integer for every v, i.e. that the grid CONTAINS the values, and then proves exactness; it says nothing about a grid that does not, which is the only case in which the procedure runs in polynomial time. The error identity with rho in {0, 1/(2D)} and the observation that the threshold in D is the value denominator are not consequences of it.
results.argument: The upper bound and the round count are immediate (monotone iteration on a finite grid; each unproductive round is a fixed point, each productive one raises a coordinate by at least 1/D). At a fixed point, (Ty)_v at an average vertex is the mean of two grid points, hence a half-integer multiple of 1/D, so rho_v = y_v - (Ty)_v lies in {0, 1/(2D)}; at a controlled vertex Ty is itself a grid point so rho_v = 0. For a player-free game y = My + b + rho gives y - w* = (I-M)^{-1} rho, i.e. the error is 1/(2D) times a Green's-function weight. What is NOT proved is that the LEAST fixed point realises a positive rho at a vertex of exponential expected-visit count on the well; that is the gap sentence recorded below.
results.verification: t_gridall.py, exact: on WELL^-(K), K = 6,8,10,12,14 (n = 10..26, w* = 1/4 exactly), y_D(v0) computed for every D in {2,...,256} together with 2^j (j <= 16), 3^j (j <= 10), 5^j (j <= 7), 6^j (j <= 6), 10^j (j <= 5). Largest tested D with y_D(v0) >= 1/2: 26, 80, 242, 625, 2048; smallest tested D with y_D(v0) < 1/2: 27, 81, 243, 729, 2187 -- that is exactly 3^{K/2} at all five sizes. On WELL^+(K) likewise y_D(v0) = 1 (error 1 - w* -> 1/4) for every D up to the same threshold, K = 4..16. On G_m of thm:vi-lower the same scheme has error only about 1/(2D) (measured for m = 3..10 and D = 2^2..2^{2m+2}), so the failure is a property of the well and not of slow value iteration as such. A random scan of 71131 small stopping games found the ratio (y_D - w*)D as large as 2.33, so the error is not bounded by 1/D.

restatements.label: cor:grid-iteration
restatements.note: That the up-rounded iteration on ANY grid stabilises after at most ND monotone rounds at a least fixed point which is an upper bound on w* is the mechanism of cor:grid-iteration (extensive rounding + cor:comparison) with its hypothesis dropped; only the behaviour of that bound off the value grid (recorded above as a gap) is new.

restatements.label: thm:few-avg
restatements.note: Applying the amplifier with eps = 4^{-a} (lem:denominator-sharp) reduces prob:main itself to Gap_{1/4} in time N * 4^{4.36 a}; this is dominated by thm:few-avg's poly(N) 2^a, so amplification never overtakes what the paper already computes -- a remark, not a result.

restatements.label: rem:no-amplification
restatements.note: That amplifying a gap delta to a constant is possible and costs Theta(1/delta) context vertices is rem:no-amplification's own sentence; the route claims only the acyclic square (thm:pg-acyclic) and the exactness of the cyclic amplifier for two-player plugs (prop:pg-ruin).

gap: On WELL^-(K) (def:pg-well with m = K/2), the least fixed point y_D of ceil_D o T reached from 0 satisfies y_D(v_0) >= 1/2 for every integer D < 3^{K/2}, although w*(v_0) = 1/4.
next_steps: (1) The single question the ladder now reduces to is: is Gap_{1/4} on stopping SSGs in P, or target-equivalent? Everything between 1/poly and 1/4, and App and Ord alongside, is that one question (thm:pg-collapse), so a route should attack Gap_{1/4} directly and stop parameterising by eps. (2) The negative side: thm:pg-acyclic bounds only contexts, i.e. black-box reductions; the open question is whether a reduction that READS THE EDGES can amplify 4^{-a} to a constant. A concrete first target: does the amplification bound survive when the s copies are allowed to SHARE vertices (a context whose calls are not disjoint copies)? The influence proof breaks exactly there, because the call outcomes stop being independent. (3) Close the gap sentence above: prove that on the well every fixed point of ceil_D o T carries rho = 1/(2D) at a vertex of expected-visit count 3^{Omega(K)}, which would make the grid iteration a fourth proved failure and would identify the value denominator as the exact threshold of every rounded scheme. (4) The acyclic optimum lies between delta^{-2} (thm:pg-acyclic) and delta^{-4.36} (the majority tower, asymptotically delta^{-3.419}); the counting obstruction described in rem:pg-acyclic suggests the truth is delta^{-3} or delta^{-3.419}, and settling it is a self-contained combinatorial question about game DAGs. (5) thm:pg-schemes leaves untouched the transport programme over Q(G) as an approximation scheme -- Q(G) is exact on every player-free game, so refuting it needs a two-player well; that is candidate (c) of the brief and is not done here.

It contains, in order: sec:pg with def:pg-maj (the majority context), lem:pg-maj (the composite's value is g(p) = 3p^2-2p^3, with the proof that every gate is read on its p-branch), lem:pg-levels (the amplification arithmetic and the level count), thm:pg-collapse (the collapse, with the many-one reduction and the size bound eps^{-4.36} N), rem:pg-collapse (what it does and does not buy); sec:pg-acyclic with def:pg-acyclic, thm:pg-influence (|V'(p)| <= sqrt(s)/(2 sqrt(p(1-p))), proved by Bessel and Cauchy-Schwarz in the p-biased basis plus an envelope argument for max-min), thm:pg-acyclic (s >= 3/(64 delta^2)), rem:pg-acyclic (where the acyclic optimum lies, and why the gap between 2 and 3.42 is a counting gap); sec:pg-well with def:pg-well, prop:pg-well (the values, exactly 1/4 and > 3/4, and the escape bound q <= 2*3^{-(h-1)} with the excursion union bound), thm:pg-schemes (the three schemes fail), rem:pg-grid (the grid iteration, with the gap sentence stated verbatim); sec:pg-ruin with prop:pg-ruin (the ruin amplifier is exact for every stopping plug, by coupling) and rem:pg-two (the two amplifiers, and the non-stopping two-player witness). The measured tables that belong to the verification fields are in RESULTS.txt in the same directory.
prior_art: From memory, flagged UNCHECKED against the sources, no web access used. (1) The majority-of-three tower is Valiant's monotone amplification of a bias, and the AND/OR variant of it is his monotone formula for majority; the exponent log 4 / log(3/2) = 3.419 for majority-of-three and log 4 / log 1.528 = 3.27 for the alternating AND/OR tower are the standard amplification exponents. What is new here is only that the tower is realised as a context of def:gate whose composite is a stopping SSG, and the use to which it is put. (2) The derivative formula dV/dp = sum_c E[d_c h] is Margulis-Russo, and the bound sum_c Inf_c <= sqrt(s) for a [0,1]-valued function at p = 1/2 is the classical level-one/Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the total influence of a monotone Boolean function (the extremal example being majority); both are proved from first principles in pg.tex, importing nothing. (3) The gambler's-ruin amplifier and the sequential probability ratio test behind its Theta(1/delta) states are classical; rem:no-amplification already credits the ruin chain. (4) That the value gap of an SSG is exponentially small and is preserved by the natural transformations is Condon's observation, already credited in rem:no-amplification. (5) Two-sided rounded value iteration is Haddad-Monmege's, already credited at cor:grid-iteration. (6) The metastable well is the standard Kramers/double-well picture for a birth-and-death chain; I know of no use of it in this literature as an approximation-hardness witness. (7) I do not recall any published polynomial-time algorithm approximating SSG values within a constant, nor any published proof that the constant-gap promise version is as hard as the exact problem; the collapse of the 1/poly regime to the constant regime is what I believe to be new, but this belief is memory only.
games_built: Every instance below is an actual mycore.G (kinds, succ) in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-promise-gap, and every check was run FROM THE GAME. (A) THE AMPLIFIER COMPOSITES A_k(G). amp.py builds M<G> as a game; t_amp.py, t_rec.py, t_gm.py, t_bf.py, dump.py run it. Checks from the game: is_stopping (the trap test of lem:trapchar) -> True in every case; the candidate value vector shown to satisfy T x = x exactly, which on a stopping game identifies it with w* (thm:contraction); and, where the strategy count allows, brute force over ALL positional pairs. Vertex counts (non-sinks): on a two-player G (1 max, 1 min, 2 avg, val 3/4) k = 1..5 gives 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096 -- the k = 1 composite (16 non-sinks, 4 max and 4 min) was ALSO solved by brute force over all 2^4 x 2^4 pairs, value 27/32 = g(3/4); on two player-free dyadic coin chains, 12, 48, 192 and 24, 96, 384; on G_m of thm:vi-lower (m = 3,4,5), k = 1..4, up to 2560 non-sinks. Files dumped: AMP_G4_k1.json (n = 32, val 8959/16384), AMP_G4_k2.json (n = 128, val 1253477906177/2199023255552), AMP_G4_k3.json (n = 512). verify_pg.py re-reads each JSON, re-runs the trap test and recomputes the value independently (linear solve for the player-free ones, brute force for small two-player ones). (B) THE RUIN COMPOSITES R_K<G>. t_ruin.py builds them as games for K = 2..6 and computes the value by brute force over all positional pairs with the trap-aware profile evaluation. Player-free plug (val 3/4): n = 6, 9, 12, 15, all stopping, ruin formula exact at every state. Two-player plug (1 max, 1 min, val 3/4): n = 8, 12, 16, 20, all stopping, exact. Two-player plug 0 max->(1,3), 1 min->(t1,2), 2 avg->(t0,t0), 3 avg->(t1,t0) of value 1/2: n = 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 for K = 2..6, is_stopping = FALSE at every K (the predicted trap), and the value is i/(K+1) at every state nonetheless. (C) THE WELLS. well.py builds WELL(K,m) as a game; checks from the game: is_stopping -> True, the exact value vector verified to satisfy T x = x, and the ruin formula cross-checked by an independent exact linear solve. Sizes: K = 4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,20 giving n = 6,10,14,18,22,26,30,34,38 non-sinks (plus 2 sinks). WELL^-(K) has val = 1/4 exactly at every size; WELL^+(K) has val 13/16, 10/13, 121/160, 91/121, 1093/1456, 820/1093, 9841/13120. Value-iteration counts, two-sided bracket widths, damped values and grid-iteration fixed points were all computed on these games in exact rational arithmetic (t_well2.py, t_well3.py, t_well4.py, t_gridall.py). Files dumped: WELL_hi_K14.json (n = 26, val 820/1093) and WELL_lo_K14.json (n = 26, val 1/4). (D) THE INFLUENCE CHECK used 4000 randomly generated acyclic CONTEXTS (not games) evaluated as H^{p,p}, which is legitimate by lem:gate; no game is claimed there.
